context.why: Stories 1 to 4 are accepted: the API reads and writes complete records, a registered type gets its endpoints, and callers authenticate with a knox token from their account pages or the portal's session. This story makes what the API says about itself true. The interactive documentation at /api/v1/docs/ and the schema at /api/v1/schema/ are generated by drf-spectacular; the static description in fairdm/api/settings.py (FAIRDM_API_DESCRIPTION) still tells callers to log in at an endpoint that no longer exists and quotes limits and page sizes as fixed numbers. The two catalogues of registered types (SampleDiscoveryView and MeasurementDiscoveryView in fairdm/api/viewsets.py) build each type's address from a fixed string, list its fields in the nested groups the registration wrote, and for a signed-in caller count records they may not see. T044 and T045 are already met and are not yours.
prior_decisions: plan D7: a drf-spectacular postprocessing hook, in a new fairdm/api/schema.py and named in SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS['POSTPROCESSING_HOOKS'] (keep drf-spectacular's own default hook in the list), appends to the schema's info.description a short section built from the live settings: how to authenticate (a token from the account pages sent as `Authorization: Token <token>`, or the portal's session), the limits in REST_FRAMEWORK['DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES'] as they are at that moment, and the default and largest page size. Read the values when the schema is generated, so a changed setting changes the text. The static FAIRDM_API_DESCRIPTION loses its login instructions and every number. The next story renames the throttle rates and adds a setting for the largest page size (FAIRDM_API_MAX_PAGE_SIZE, read by fairdm/api/pagination.py): write the hook so it lists whatever rates are configured without knowing their names, and reads the page sizes from the pagination class. Tests assert that the configured values appear in the description and follow an overridden setting, never the wording around them.

T047: the schema's securitySchemes are the knox token header (drf-spectacular's own knox extension provides it; story 4 confirmed no extension of ours is needed) and the session cookie, and nothing for the removed mechanisms.

T046: every route the router serves has a path in the schema, and for each registered demonstration type the schema component's properties match the serializer's fields, with required and readOnly as the serializer has them. Carried from story 3: the schema still lists a content-type filter (`polymorphic_ctype`) as a query parameter on sample and measurement lists although the API ignores it and it takes a database number. The schema must not list it or any other parameter the API does not act on (see decisions.md D20 for why the filter is removed per request and not on the class; fix it so the schema agrees, for example by excluding it where the schema reads the filter set, without breaking the portal's own pages that share the filter set).

plan D3, catalogues: each entry's address is reverse() of the type's list route made absolute with request.build_absolute_uri, never a string put together by hand; `fields` is the flat list the type's API serializer actually carries; filters are the parameters the API's filter set for that type accepts; `count` is the number of records the caller may see, obtained by running the type's queryset through FairDMVisibilityFilter (fairdm/api/filters.py) for a visitor, a signed-in person with no level and someone with a level on a private dataset. Keep the existing keys of an entry where they still make sense so the shape stays recognisable, and say in the report which keys changed.
T050: the API root at /api/v1/ links to every list route and both catalogues (FairDMAPIRouter.get_api_root_view in fairdm/api/router.py already adds the catalogue links; prove it for all of them).

T051 also deletes the setting FAIRDM_API_DOCS_URL from fairdm/api/settings.py and from the import and __all__ lists in fairdm/conf/settings/api.py (nothing reads it since the sidebar was reduced to one link), and deletes TestFairDMAPIDocsURLSetting in tests/test_api/test_settings.py. In tests/test_menus/test_menus.py, change the API menu test so it counts the entries leading to the documentation page across the whole menu and expects exactly one, without relying on the entry's position; that edit to an existing test is authorised. Tests in tests/test_api/test_router.py or test_settings.py that pin the old catalogue shape or the old static description describe behaviour this story replaces: update them and name each in progress.md.

T052 documentation: the documentation page, the schema address, the catalogues and what each entry holds, in docs/portal-development/restful-api.md and the page for people using a portal. Remove any mention of FAIRDM_API_DOCS_URL from docs/.
Update feature-state.json for your own tasks (status, attempts, evidence with tests, commands, code as path:line, verified_by_ci) and tick your tasks in tasks.md.
No architecture decision record is needed for this story.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the router's routes and the registered types, when the schema is generated, then every route has a path, each type's component matches its serializer's fields with required and read-only marked, and no parameter is listed that the API ignores.
Given the schema, then its security schemes are the token header and the session, and its description carries the configured limits and page sizes and follows a changed setting.
Given the catalogues, then each registered type is listed with its name, an address equal to its list route, a flat field list and its filters, and with no registered types the list is empty.
Given a private dataset with records, then a catalogue's count is what a visitor, a signed-in person with no level, and someone with a level may each see.
Given the API root, then it links to every list route and both catalogues.
Given the failing tests from T046 to T050, when the implementation lands, then they pass, FAIRDM_API_DOCS_URL is gone and the menu test counts entries.
Given the documentation pages, when read against the branch, then they describe the documentation page, the schema and the catalogues as they now are.
